title: Introduce KMS consent telemetry and RBAC shadow checker
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes:
- Add KMS consent telemetry events (consent_event.v1) for policy decisions and key usage.
- Add RBAC v2 shadow checker that evaluates policy diffs without enforcing to detect regression risks.
- New dashboards: consent-entropy and shadow-checker-delta.
- Migration CLI to bulk-run shadow checks against historical audit samples.
description:
Background and motivation: Customers and compliance teams have asked for better visibility into when requests fall back to alternative KMS providers or when operator-scoped RBAC rules would have blocked operations in a future RBAC v2 rollout. This PR adds two complementary pieces: (1) structured KMS consent telemetry emitted whenever a KMS routing decision or consent check is taken, and (2) a non-enforcing RBAC shadow checker that replays live decisions (and historical audit samples) against RBAC v2 policies to surface policy deltas, false positives, and drift before we flip the enforcement bit.

Design summary: The telemetry layer emits a new schema (consent_event.v1) with fields: request_id, tenant_id, service_zone, kms_provider, consent_decision (allow/deny/fallback), decision_reason, latency_ms, operator_claims (list), and a consent_entropy bucket (computed per-tennant window). Events are coalesced by the audit coalescer to reduce noise for noisy paths (e.g., orchestration heartbeats). The RBAC shadow checker runs inline as a sidecar-enabled library call in the auth path when the feature flag rbac_shadow_enabled=true, and also as an offline migrator CLI that consumes audit logs and writes diffs to rbac-shadow/{date} index for analysis.

Commits (high level):
- add: pkg/kms/consent_telemetry.go + api schema for consent_event.v1
- add: internal/audit/coalescer.go to group low-value events
- add: cmd/rbac-shadow-runner for offline replay against RBAC v2 rules
- add: auth/shadow_checker.go integrating dry-run RBAC evaluation
- docs: docs/security/kms-consent-telemetry.md and migration guide
- infra: helm values and dashboard jsonnet for consent-entropy

Changed areas (high level):
- pkg/kms/ (telemetry hooks and minor refactors)
- internal/auth/ (shadow checker implementation and unit tests)
- internal/audit/ (coalescer and event sink registration)
- cmd/ (new migration tool to run shadow checks in bulk)
- observability/ (dashboards and alerts)
- docs/ (security and migration guide)

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for consent_event serialization and for the shadow checker decision engine. Integration test that spins up a minimal auth + fake-kms backend and asserts both emitted telemetry and shadow diffs. A small e2e run was executed against the staging audit stream with 10k events (sampled) to validate memory and disk footprint of the coalescer. Initial CI run failed due to a flaky clock-dependent test (auth/tokens_test). Flaky assertion fixed by using a deterministic clock stub; full CI re-run passed (all checks green).

Performance: Microbenchmarks show ~1.8% median added latency on the critical auth path when the inline shadow checker is enabled; due to this we gate the inline checker behind a per-cluster feature flag and recommend starting with the offline runner for large tenants. The consent telemetry path is async and uses buffered batching to keep tail latency impact negligible.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Step 1 (canary): Deploy to staging and two small production clusters with rbac_shadow_enabled=false and telemetry enabled for KMS service routes only.
- Step 2 (shadow): Enable rbac_shadow_enabled=true in a canary cluster; run the offline runner against 30d of audit samples to build a baseline.
- Step 3 (policy review): Use the rbac-shadow index and the generated deltas dashboard to triage policy false positives; update policy templates as needed.
- Step 4 (enforce): Targeted gradual enforcement after 2 weeks of no-high-risk deltas.

Operational notes and backward compatibility: The new event schema is versioned (v1) and emitted under the existing audit topic. Coalescer reduces event volume for high-cardinality tenants; customers can opt-out via tenant config (audit_coalesce=false). RBAC shadow checker does not change enforcement behavior unless the rollout flag rbac_enforce_v2=true. The offline runner includes a dry-run mode and outputs a signed report for compliance teams.

Security considerations: Consent events include operator claims and service_zone but redact raw PII; the telemetry pipeline is integrated with KMS usage tagging so event retention follows tenant retention policies. The offline runner accesses historical audit logs and requires the new role: role:rbac_shadow_runner (documented in the migration guide).

Related work and references: Linear ENG-8194 (RBAC shadowing MVP) and ENG-8271 (KMS consent telemetry). See docs/security/kms-consent-telemetry.md for schema and example queries.

This description is intentionally condensed; refer to changed files for implementation details and the migration guide for step-by-step instructions.
